name: jevsubrouter
description: JevSubRouter is a dependency-free Claude Code plugin whose hooks route each sub-agent dispatch to the cheapest sufficient model tier—without touching the orchestrator's cached prefix—with fail-open routing, worker background context, and /jev-why/jev-stats observability.

name: compact-adviser
description: compact-adviser is a plugin for Pi, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Grok that scores each settled turn via TypeSafe's Jev model against a context-fill-adjusted threshold to hint—or, where supported and opted in, automatically run—/compact when the session reaches a safe boundary.

name: dlq_inspector
description: Local-first CLI for inspecting RabbitMQ and Redis Streams dead-letter queues: it groups failures by cause, then recovers messages only through dry-run plans, explicit --confirm, and rate limits—snapshotting replays for rollback and logging every action to a local audit trail.

name: skills
description: A collection of agent skills for building with TypeSafe's System One API, giving coding agents reusable guidance and workflows that make it easier to integrate and work with the API correctly.

name: jev-llm
description: jev-llm coerces TypeSafe Jev — a judgment/classification engine — into an autoregressive language model by decoding token-by-token through multiple-choice candidate selection, offering word, char, hybrid, and syntax-aware code generation modes with temperature sampling, planning, and interactive chat.

name: vgi-typesafe
description: A DuckDB extension worker exposing TypeSafe System One question primitives—choice, noul, and score—as table functions that classify, rate, or filter rows via LATERAL joins, returning typed columns including per-answer confidence for routing decisions, with multi-question ask() calls, per-row dynamic questions, scalar is_true() filtering, and bind-time validation.

name: Jevbridge
description: Jevbridge is a zero-dependency Node 22 library and MCP/ACP stdio adapter that pairs any LLM with TypeSafe Jev's typed System One decisions (noul, choice, score), confidence-gating tool calls and closed-set computer-use actions so software can branch on probabilistic answers.

name: open-jev-typed-decision-engine
description: An open 150M ModernBERT encoder that answers arbitrary per-request typed questions (boolean, choice, score) about a state in one forward pass with calibrated confidences, trainable free on a Colab T4, scoring 0.697 accuracy vs TypeSafe Jev's 0.727 at ~60ms locally.

name: grok-bot-jev
description: A Python router that classifies Grok Bot requests via TypeSafe Jev's `system_one` call, returning explicit actions (reuse_cache, stop_retry, research_capped, ask_human) so shadow or active modes can skip needless browser, retry, research, or subagent work.

name: jev-demo
description: A Next.js demo dashboard that triages GitHub issues into five typed Jev-1.13 decisions—category, severity, urgency, team, and actionability—with calibrated confidence thresholds, live timing/cost metrics, and Kanban or action-based views for automatic routing versus human review.

name: jev-nethack
description: Public source, live gameplay viewer, archived recordings, and research artifacts for Jev, an AI agent persistently playing NetHack — including the runner, crash-recovery background service, BC/PPO training pilots, sanitized transition datasets, and rigorously documented negative-result experiments.

name: noflow-runtime
description: noflow-runtime is a React 18+ package where buttons report their label and DOM context to a pluggable policy (local mock, HTTP, or server-side Jev) that selects only among app-registered affordances, with runtime safety gates for confidence thresholds, user confirmation, and error fallbacks.

name: hermes-jev-skills
description: Eight agent-agnostic skills and a Hermes plugin that delegate per-turn decisions—model routing, memory filtering, compaction, skill selection, triage, GUI/browser actions—to TypeSafe's Jev decision model (~0.4 s, ~$0.00006), with redacted payloads and fail-open fallbacks.

name: winnow
description: Winnow is a Claude Code plugin that intercepts large Read/Bash/Grep outputs, uses a calibrated probability judge to hide blocks unlikely to matter for the current task—replacing them with summarized stubs restorable via a recall key—and injects prompt-relevant memory files, cutting token costs without losing content.

name: system-one-benchmark
description: A benchmarking suite that compares TypeSafe Jev's cloud "System One" decision model against local MLX parallel constrained decoding and autoregressive Qwen baselines on adversarial and intent prompts, measuring latency, accuracy, safety precision/recall, calibration, and schema-error rates.

name: jev-preflight
description: A Claude Code plugin that snapshots a private Git baseline each turn and sends the redacted diff to TypeSafe's Jev API, scoring eight risk axes so high-risk changes get one focused re-investigation before finishing, while failing open on errors.

name: jev-tetris
description: A dependency-free Node/browser Tetris played by a textless multiple-choice model: the engine enumerates every legal placement, describes each in prose, JEV returns per-option probabilities, and the board visualizes preference and confidence, with mock mode, tests, and benchmark controls included.

name: jevs-kitchen-chaos
description: Jev's Kitchen Chaos is a live Overcooked-style 3D benchmark arena where four AI chefs make streamed API decisions, letting users swap decision models/LLMs and compare score, latency, policy, confidence, token cost, and downloadable decision logs.

name: jevscan-evm
description: A Python CLI that scans Solidity/EVM repos via TypeSafe's Jev, running 343 detectors across 14 vulnerability categories to output a color-coded HEATMAP.md scoring each file's bug likelihood and flagging suspect functions with confidence percentages for fast, cheap pre-audit triage.

name: purelink
description: A browser extension that scores LinkedIn posts for AI authorship using a lightweight decision model answering 17 weighted questions instead of an LLM, flags engagement/curiosity/rage bait, and offers an on-demand fact-checker that annotates claims in place with sourced verdicts.

name: ailang-packages
description: A monorepo of tested, reusable AILANG packages extracted from production projects, providing modules for GCP auth, HTTP helpers, logging, config, Firestore, billing/Stripe, contract reasoning, and typed decisions, installable via registry, path, or git-subdir dependencies.

name: jev-codex-plugin
description: An open-source Codex plugin that provides TypeSafe Jev decision consultation, failure diagnosis, and completion-evidence review through MCP tools, lifecycle hooks, and standalone CLI skills, returning recommendations or abstentions without acting automatically.

name: typesafe-sdk-go
description: An unofficial Go SDK for the TypeSafe AI API that provides a configurable client, typed SystemOne questions and choice/score/noul answers, model listing, structured API errors, and runnable live-API examples.

name: neo4jev
description: neo4jev is a schema-agnostic Python library (with notebooks and a Streamlit app) that navigates any Neo4j graph one hop at a time via TypeSafe's `system_one` API, using beam search over per-hop Choice/Noul probability distributions to find best-scoring paths and render them with `neo4j-viz`.

name: pr-sieve
description: pr-sieve is a GitHub Action that treats a base-ref `.jev.yml` of typed TypeSafe Jev questions as a semantic PR linter, failing, commenting, or passing check runs on scored answers plus code-level secret detection—never writing reviews or approving changes.

name: jev-market-reflex
description: A Bun/TypeScript demo that streams live Kraken BTC/ETH/SOL market data into TypeSafe AI Jev, converts compact market features into typed BUY/SELL/HOLD decisions with confidence and probabilities, and applies deterministic risk-gated paper execution with simulated P&L to a browser dashboard—no real funds or exchange credentials required.

name: jev-reviewer
description: Browser-based systematic review tool that answers extraction-form questions across a study's files (PDF, Word, Excel, slides, etc.) with verbatim, located quotes selected—not generated—by the Jev model, plus checking, an extraction table, PRISMA reporting, and local-only storage.

name: jev-precheck
description: jev-precheck is an MCP proxy that forwards reads untouched but, before each write, fetches affected records and computes comparisons in code so Jev can flow, warn, or hold well-formed but wrong calls like duplicate payments or oversized credit notes.

name: jev-cli
description: jev-cli installs `jev` and `jev-mcp`—a CLI and stdio MCP server—that send text/JSON state to TypeSafe Jev and return machine-readable noul, choice, or score judgments, with batching, multi-provider auth, and script-friendly output for fast classification without generated prose.

name: llm-rankers
description: A Python toolkit for LLM-based document reranking implementing pointwise (yes/no, QLM), listwise sliding-window, pairwise, and efficient Setwise sorting methods over pyserini BM25 runs, supporting FLAN-T5, monoT5/duoT5, OpenAI models, and Rank-R1, with TREC DL/BEIR examples.

name: openevals
description: An online eval service that grades every trace and every step of production agent traffic with cheap, fast typed jev questions, writes scores back to Langfuse, and supports custom rubrics, deterministic checks, and human-annotation calibration—all in one process and one SQLite file.

name: jevocks
description: A Bloomberg-style terminal that retrieves live market, news, analyst, and macro evidence through five parallel Valyu searches, then uses TypeSafe AI's Jev System One evaluation model to estimate the probability a stock trades higher in 30 days, reporting category signals, sources, and timing.

name: maza
description: Maza is a local Node.js MCP gateway that aggregates multiple MCP servers behind a single endpoint, exposing only `find_tool` and `execute_tool` to agents while centrally managing connections, OS-stored credentials, per-tool enablement, client allowlists, and bearer-token authentication.

name: eslint-plugin-jev
description: An ESLint plugin that goes beyond conventional linters' structural checks by analyzing what code actually means, enabling it to catch semantic issues that shape-only linting cannot detect.

name: jev-block-android-ad
description: An Android noise gate that funnels notifications and SMS through one pipeline — local OTP gate and sender blacklist first, then a model given channel history and user rules — suppressing only flagged ads while every uncertain path fails open.

name: typesafe-jev-tools
description: A Claude Code PreToolUse hook that scans JS/TS/Python writes and edits for LLM calls and hand-written classifiers, then injects a three-way test—plain code, frontier model, or a fast uncertainty-aware judgment model like Jev—so decisions that a regex could answer don't silently ship as brittle heuristics or overqualified model calls.

name: jevinize
description: A Claude Code skill that transforms a described use case into a working classifier/router system powered by simple-jev, scaffolding the routing logic that directs inputs to the appropriate handler.

name: jev-legal-instrumentation-latam
description: A reproducible Spanish-language pilot benchmarking typed-decision classification on 30 public Argentine Supreme Court metadata records—comparing deterministic rules, a local 0.5B model, and the Jev SDK—to show that high model confidence does not equal legal correctness.

name: opencode-plugin-variantizer
description: An OpenCode v1 plugin that uses TypeSafe to automatically route each request to one of three fixed-model agents (luna, terra, or sol) and select a reasoning variant (none through max), with configurable fallbacks, confidence-aware notifications, secret-tool credential support, and pre-provider validation to prevent silent mismatches.

name: jevmetrics
description: `jevmetrics` is an experimental OpenTelemetry Collector connector that asynchronously calls TypeSafe's Jev model to score metric instruments' operational value from their metadata, then applies cached, threshold-based keep/drop policy to annotate or filter metrics before export.

name: typesafe-mcp
description: A Go binary `evaluate` that runs a stdio MCP server exposing one read-only tool: coding agents send observed state plus typed noul/choice/score questions to TypeSafe Jev (or OpenRouter) and get back probabilities, choices, and scores to branch on in code.

name: jev-android-super
description: An Android app that completes plain-English goals on a phone by reading the accessibility UI tree, requesting ~400 ms typed actions from TypeSafe's Jev model (Gemini/OpenRouter for text), performing real taps, with STOP, purchase-block, and loop-detection safeguards.

name: laterhook
description: Laterhook is a self-hosted webhook inbox that captures every request sent to zero-setup endpoints, then lets you inspect, search, replay, tag, secure, and permanently forward matching traffic through regex routes before your real backend is ready.

name: pg-jev
description: pg-jev is a PostgreSQL extension that lets you filter, rank, and classify table rows with plain-language conditions via SQL functions (`jev`, `jev_prob`, `jev_score`, `jev_choice`), where each row is judged by TypeSafe's Jev model returning calibrated probabilities—no index, embeddings, or vector column required.

name: jarviscore-framework
description: JarvisCore is an Apache-2.0 Python runtime for multi-agent systems: agents discover each other over a SWIM gossip mesh, claim crash-durable workflow steps from Redis (surviving `kill -9`), and invoke 150+ services through a zero-trust credential vault — no central orchestrator.

name: feedwall
description: Feedwall is a dependency-free Manifest V3 browser extension for Chrome-based browsers that filters feeds on X, YouTube, Reddit, LinkedIn, and Hacker News by sending each post to a fast yes/no-probability model (TypeSafe's Jev) under your own API key, letting you define custom plain-English topics with Keep/Hide/Dim/Highlight actions, per-site focus mode, a test-on-recent-posts preview, mistake fee

name: pi-warden
description: pi-warden supervises Pi coding sessions by checking commands, edits, replies, and subagent reports for risky actions, rule violations, stuck loops, unverified “done” claims, secrets, runaway output, and noise, steering the agent to self-correct or holding irreversible steps.

name: simple-jev
description: Simple Jev is a local Hugging Face/PyTorch server that turns shared context plus choice, rubric-score, or truth questions into JSON answers by scoring next-token logits, reusing the common prompt’s KV cache to avoid generated completions and repeated prefill.

name: pi-jev-sentinel
description: A guard for coding agents that uses TypeSafe's Jev model to judge each tool call's intent and risk, screen tool outputs for prompt injection, and check finished replies—shipping as a Pi extension and as Claude Code/Codex CLI hooks, with secret scrubbing.

name: jev-macos-loop
description: Jev macOS Loop is an open-source Apple-silicon tool for native macOS GUI automation that uses local CoreML detection, OCR, and accessibility with Jev decisions while keeping screenshots and coordinates on-device.

name: jev-311-heatmap
description: A tool that generates interactive geographic heatmaps of NYC 311 complaints through a reproducible TypeSafe JEV pipeline, letting users explore live research results and complaint patterns across the city.

name: chess-jev
description: ChessJev scores chess moves by keeping legal-move generation in python-chess and ranking UCI candidates with a one-pass MiniLM or byte-level model, served through a local FastAPI app with selectable scorers and scripts to finetune on Stockfish-labeled positions.

name: typesafe-mario
description: TypeSafe Mario is a Python harness that lets TypeSafe's Jev model play Super Mario Bros. by parsing emulator RAM into structured JSON describing Mario's motion, hazards, terrain, and timing, then translating the model's Choice/Noul/Score judgments into controller inputs, with a live telemetry dashboard and per-decision JSONL logging.

name: jevscan
description: jevscan is a CLI, library, and MCP server that turns an EVM token contract address into typed `ape / watch / avoid` verdicts with calibrated probabilities plus `rug_risk`, `momentum`, `liquidity_health`, and `fdv_stress` scores — deterministic local engine by default, swappable to the TypeSafe jev endpoint with an API key, and grep-style exit codes make it a pipeable gate for buy scripts and scr

name: mobile-jev
description: Mobile Jev is a standalone agent that drives a real Android phone through the Mobilerun API (no ADB), with TypeSafe's Jev choosing each action toward a natural-language goal, plus a live React studio, CLI, execution traces, and latency measurements for verification.

name: typesafe-sdk-python
description: Python SDK for TypeSafe AI that installs via `uv add typesafe-sdk` and provides a `TypeSafeClient` (authenticated via `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) whose `system_one` method classifies input state into structured `Choice` categories defined by instructions and criteria, returning typed results.

name: tg_accessor
description: CLI toolkit that exports Telegram group history to CSV, narrows it to one user's messages plus context, uses TypeSafe to stitch messages into topical threads scored for conflict and convincingness, and rolls it up into a per-user PROFILE.md.

name: jev-browser-qa
description: A Playwright browser-QA toolkit where the fast Jev model answers yes/no and one-of questions to power natural-language assertions, intent-based element picking, and goal-driven click loops, with a JSON CLI, recorded video/traces, and a local run-history dashboard.

name: JevFish
description: JevFish is an OASIS-based social-simulation runtime that turns seed inputs into agent societies, uses TypeSafe Jev for fast typed multi-action decisions, invokes generative models only when needed, and provides A/B benchmarks and metrics for scalable outcome analysis.

name: typesafe-ai-php
description: A PHP 8.2+ client for the TypeSafe AI evaluation API that lets you send a state plus typed questions (yes/no "noul", multiple-choice, ordered "score") via a fluent `EvaluationRequest` and read back typed answers with probabilities, confidence, and token usage—handling retries, errors, and debug logging automatically.

name: jev-guard
description: jev-guard is a cross-agent PreToolUse hook (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity) that intercepts shell, file, and patch operations to enforce workspace boundaries and sensitive-file protection via a sub-1ms local fastpath plus TypeSafe AI's Jev model for semantic blast-radius/destructiveness evaluation, with enforcing and audit modes and fail-safe blocking under autonomous bypass flags.

name: jev-ios-ultrafast
description: A Python CLI and Brigade host wrapper that runs goal-driven iOS Simulator tasks via Jev, benchmarks decision models against each other, and records every attempt for replay — enabling automated UI testing and systematic model comparison.

name: WindTunnel
description: WindTunnel is a benchmark harness that runs identical seeded tasks on self-hosted real web apps, comparing WebMCP against screenshot, DOM/accessibility-tree, and code-execution interfaces for browser agents via outcome-based scoring of success, time, tokens, and cost.

name: jev-prune-kit
description: jev-prune-kit provides a capability-aware context-pruning installer, a bounded Jev assessment engine, and experimental request-projection adapters for harness integration, enabling controlled context reduction and evaluation workflows that remain experimental and untested on live hosts.

name: mcp_typesafe
description: An MCP server exposing TypeSafe's System One (Jev) API as 12 tools that return fast (~100 ms), calibrated, structured judgments—probabilities, choices, scores, and confidence—enabling agents to filter, rank, classify, dedupe, verify, and select items in bulk without text generation or parsing.

name: jev-tweet-radar
description: A Chrome MV3 extension that scores each X timeline post and your drafts with one Jev (TypeSafe System One) API call, showing calibrated probabilities for engagement-worthiness and tags like spam/buzz/AI-ish, with goal-aware judging, opacity-based timeline filtering, reply-context scoring, and per-day cost tracking.

name: vercel-jev-mcp
description: A Hono-based remote MCP server deployable to Vercel that relays Bearer-authenticated evaluation calls (jev_ask, jev_classify, jev_score, jev_check) through Vercel AI Gateway to TypeSafe Jev, letting multiple AI clients share one URL without Jev API keys.

name: JEV-EFMW-Syncretic-Layer
description: Reproducible synthetic testbed simulating a Jev-like typed decision layer with an EFMW-style recursive coherence monitor, providing three controlled experiments—calibration degradation, closed-loop trajectory instability, and an equal-information anti-circularity comparison—run via pip, Python scripts, and pytest under frozen null-calibrated thresholds.

name: jev-1.13-mini-benchmark
description: A self-contained benchmark harness that evaluates the jev-1.13 structured decision model on 34 labeled support-triage cases across its noul/choice/score question types, with offline scoring, threshold sweeps, confusion matrices, and consistency checks on a swappable dataset.

name: ruby_decision_model
description: Ruby gem that answers typed questions (noul, choice, score) about a state with calibrated probabilities via one Client backed by OpenRouter or Typesafe, with retries, model aliases, pluggable transports, and typed errors—no runtime dependencies.

name: jev-gamepilot
description: jev-gamepilot is an autonomous AI gaming agent that captures any live Windows game (browser, Steam, or emulator) at 60+ FPS, queries TypeSafe's Jev System One model for tactical decisions via built-in or custom profiles, and executes real keyboard/mouse inputs with emergency stop fail-safes.

name: site-judge
description: A CI check that audits marketing site copy for unsupported claims, combining deterministic regex checks with a probability-returning judgment model validated per-run by known-good/known-bad controls, and reports each flagged claim's sentence and score as an advisory, never-blocking PR comment.

name: jev-mcp
description: MCP server exposing ten fast, low-cost judgment tools (verify, screen, find, rerank, classify, decide, compare, extract, review, gate) that return typed probabilities and confidence scores so agents can fact-check claims, detect prompt injection, rank candidates, and validate diffs without a frontier model.

name: jeff
description: jeff is a self-hosted implementation of TypeSafe's jev System One API powered by the 400M-parameter GLiFormer model, serving SDK-compatible choice, score, and noul classification endpoints more cheaply than jev, though less accurately on reasoning-heavy tasks.

name: jev-adblocker
description: jev-adblocker is an ad-blocking tool that filters or suppresses advertisements, helping users reduce unwanted ad content during browsing or related workflows.

name: oxlint-plugin-jev
description: An oxlint plugin that turns plain-English yes/no questions about functions, calls, JSX elements, or whole files into lint rules—TypeSafe Jev returns a probability per match and reports an error at your configured cutoff, with per-file batching, answer caching, and CI fail/skip controls.

name: OpenWhisper
description: OpenWhisper is a cross-platform desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux that provides hotkey-driven dictation, audio-file transcription, and meeting capture with live dashboards using local speech models (Whisper, Parakeet, Qwen3-ASR, Moonshine) or the OpenAI API, plus AI text cleanup, searchable history, and export.

name: typesafe-image-diffusion
description: Generates 16x16 pixel art from text prompts by asking a multiple-choice classifier 256 parallel questions—one per pixel choosing among 16 colors—with optional local-neighborhood refinement passes, served via a FastAPI web UI and API with animated history and token usage.

name: typesafe-local
description: A local server that answers typed questions (yes/no, choice, score) about a document by encoding it once into a reusable KV cache and softmaxing a single position's logits over legal answer tokens, returning calibrated probability distributions instead of generated text.

name: llm-skills
description: Agent skills (SKILL.md + templates) for Cursor/Claude Code/Antigravity/Codex covering benchmark-verified local LLM selection with VRAM checks and Jev deterministic-model design—candidate detection, TCO estimation, typed schemas, fallbacks, eval-set freeze, calibration, observability.

name: unclutter
description: WXT browser extension for Chrome/Chromium and Firefox that uses the Jev AI model (with your own Vercel AI Gateway or TypeSafe AI key) to hide nonessential page elements via reusable per-template rules cached locally, with manual or on-visit analysis and pause/resume controls.

name: azdaja
description: Azdaja is a recursive language-model layer that keeps full inputs in a persistent local Monty/Python evaluator, giving models a bounded surface for local computation and selective llm/llm_batch recursion—cutting tokens and steps—with optional TypeSafe typed judgments.

name: kev
description: kev is a local decision-model server — a LoRA adapter plus pointer readout head on a Qwen base (0.5B–8B) — that answers many typed questions (yes/no, multi-choice, ordinal score) about a document in one decode-free prefill pass, returning calibrated softmax probabilities through a TypeSafe System One–compatible API.

name: JevRouter
description: JevRouter is a TypeScript/Node.js routing layer that uses the Jev decision model to select among models, subagents, skills, MCP tools, CLIs, and plugins—reducing reasoning-token overhead while enforcing availability, permissions, risk, confirmation, and auditable single- or multi-step plans.

name: reranker
description: A reranker that scores up to 30 documents in a single call using TypeSafe's Jev model, returning a calibrated probability per document, distributed under the Apache-2.0 license.

name: jev-vpn
description: Jev-VPN is a Windows privacy proxy that blocks ads, trackers, telemetry, and malvertising at the socket layer using static blocklists and AI domain triage, with one-click system-wide routing, an encrypted tunnel, and GUI/CLI live metrics.

name: thiscita-typesafe
description: OBRA is a Next.js 15/TypeScript workspace demonstrating typed AI decisions via the TypeSafe SDK across three bilingual tools—government services search, PDF/DOCX/TXT proposal review with deterministic readiness scoring, and a voice-enabled personal agenda—keeping LLM classification separate from rule-based execution with server-side key handling and no document persistence.

name: magic-8-ball
description: A Vite/TypeScript Magic 8 Ball whose Cloudflare Worker relays each question to TypeSafe's `systemone` Choice API, letting `jev-latest` pick one of twenty witty replies rendered in a CSS-only ball with true latency timing, rate limiting, and deploy tooling.

name: jev-plays-games
description: A Node.js web app that lets you play chess or Connect Four against the Jev language model (or watch it play itself) via OpenRouter, describing board state and legal moves as a multiple-choice question and displaying the model's move probabilities, confidence, and per-turn cost.

name: jev-downloads-sorter
description: A macOS launchd agent that watches ~/Downloads and uses Jev decisions, with an offline extension-map fallback, to route each finished file or folder into your configured folders without overwrites using filename, type, size, source URL, and content hints.

name: jev-k8s-awareness
description: A proof-of-concept real-time Kubernetes cluster awareness dashboard that uses an informer to watch pods in a namespace, evaluates unhealthy pods via TypeSafe Jev for severity, remediation, and escalation, and streams results to a browser UI over SSE.

name: JevSwiftSDK
description: A dependency-free Swift package wrapping TypeSafe's Jev decision-model HTTP API, providing a Sendable async client that evaluates state against typed Choice, Score, and Noul questions—individually, in batches, or via reusable question sets—with environment or explicit configuration, retries, per-request options, structured JSON state, and granular error handling.

name: jev-pii-checker
description: jev-pii-checker is a CLI that scans stdin/files for PII using TypeSafe's Jev API, regexes, and Intl.Segmenter name-span assembly, emitting masked JSON or human reports with severity exit codes to gate sensitive text before LLM use—at the cost of sending scanned content to TypeSafe.

name: JevML
description: JevML is a dependency-free TypeScript toolkit of reusable ML primitives—PCA, MCMC sampling, text diffusion, and neural cellular automata—with a catalog/registry and matching/API harness that helps agents select and invoke the right primitive for a task.

name: jev-use
description: jev-use is a macOS voice-and-typed computer-use agent that reads the Accessibility tree instead of screenshots, lets an LLM pick each on-screen action, executes presses, typing, menus, scrolling and window arrangement, and verifies real effects in a loop until done.

name: Jev-StepPilot
description: A Windows-only Tauri desktop agent that autonomously carries out a typed goal by watching the active window and asking Jev for each next step—launching apps via Start-menu search, pausing on uncertain or hard-to-undo actions, and aborting when the mouse hits a screen corner.

name: jev-align
description: A CLI/MCP/programmable verifier that scores every LLM response or agent plan on calibrated alignment heads (sycophancy, deception, overreach, sneaking, etc.) in ~800ms for ~$0.003, returning auditable probabilities and pass/flag/block verdicts enforceable via CI exit codes.

name: hunch
description: A Ruby gem providing probabilistic control flow primitives—`chance`, `pick`, and `rate`—that let programs branch, select, and sample randomly, powered by TypeSafe's Jev.

name: readybase-public
description: ReadyBase is a local-first CLI that maps repo dependencies, blast radius, ownership, and conventions to score AI-readiness, flag drift in AI-written code, guard risky edits, and certify the autonomy level (L0–L3) a codebase can safely support.

name: jev-mcp
description: jev-mcp is a local stdio MCP server that gives hosts like Cursor and Codex nine typed TypeSafe Jev judgment tools — for routing steps, selecting prepared tool calls, reviewing patches, verifying claims, screening content, ranking candidates, and gating — returning Choice/Score/Noul answers with confidence and auto/review/escalate actions while the host executes tools itself.

name: doc-router
description: doc-router is a Rust CLI/library that inspects PDFs page-by-page to extract text-layer pages locally while sending only genuinely scanned pages to an OCR provider via LiteLLM, merging results into a page-ordered output that cut measured OCR cost 1.74x and latency 1.72x.

name: jev-router
description: jev-router is a loopback proxy that wraps the Claude Code and OpenAI Codex CLIs, sending each fresh user turn to a Jev routing call that picks a fast, balanced, strong, or long model tier while preserving native sessions, tools, auth, and manual model-picker overrides.

name: decider
description: decider is a fine-tuned language model that reads a state plus typed questions (choice, score, yes/no) and returns calibrated probabilities over the answer options in one forward pass—no decoding—served via a cached, TypeSafe-compatible HTTP API for fast structured decisions.

name: jev-cli
description: jev-cli (`jev`, npm package `jevctl`) wraps TypeSafe's Jev model to return fast, cheap probabilistic judgments—verify claims, screen for prompt injection, classify, extract, rerank, match, route—via scriptable commands with JSON output and exit codes for gating CI.

name: AssertLens
description: AssertLens is a dependency-free Node 24.12+ CLI that runs sandboxed executable checks (via Bubblewrap on Linux) against Git working trees or commits and sends selected files' before/after contents with named falsifiable assertions to the Jev model for advisory supported/contradicted/insufficient verdicts in local and GitHub PR workflows.

name: openjev
description: Open-source, Jev-compatible "System One" decision server: answers typed questions (yes/no, choice, score) about a state or images with calibrated probabilities in tens of milliseconds, plus OpenAI-compatible text generation, served by DiffusionGemma via vLLM.

name: is-malicious
description: A Node.js CLI that sends a project's source, config, build, and CI files to the TypeSafe Jev API to flag hidden, deceptive, or data-stealing behavior, reporting suspicious file/line locations with severity, token cost, and CI-ready exit codes for local or PR-diff scans.

name: mario-never-dies
description: A demo that uses microsandbox VM snapshots to checkpoint a running Mario game every 150 frames and, on each death, branches the last checkpoint into four VM copies racing different recoveries so the survivor becomes the run, while the Jev API picks moves from parsed RAM state and a browser visualizes the branching timelines.

name: zammad-jev-dispatcher
description: A Zammad integration that uses Jev (TypeSafe AI) to automatically triage incoming tickets, classifying each one and routing it to the appropriate service group so support teams can skip manual sorting and reach the right queue faster.

name: SemIf

name: jev-browser

name: jev-voice-browser

description: TypeAR is a constrained-decoding client for SGLang-served open autoregressive LLMs that yields type-safe outputs (single-token enum/boolean choices, bounded numeric values, free text) via sequential or prefix-cached batch execution, with optional thinking, sampling, and per-choice probabilities.

name: joxide

name: jev-browser

name: Jev-Radar

name: jev-extraction-marker-recovery
description: A Python script that recovers footnote and citation markers lost when OCR flattens superscripts, using a recall-heavy tokenizer to surface suspicious tokens and Jev (TypeSafe) to classify each as citation, footnote, section label, unit/exponent, or non-marker for reinsertion.

name: TypeSafe

description: sqlite-jev is a SQLite loadable extension and Python package adding natural-language predicates, classification, and scoring to SQL via TypeSafe Jev, including a batched `jev_rows` virtual table joinable by rowid, scalar functions, connection-local caching, and spend guards.

name: jev-playground

name: djev-spark

name: openagents

name: dinostomp

description: A Rust CLI that pipes unstructured operational signals (logs, journal entries, Kubernetes events, cloud telemetry) through declarative, security-sandboxed YAML diagnostic packs to TypeSafe Jev inference, returning typed probabilistic decisions (category, severity, attention) with confidence scores for gating alerts and auto-remediation.

name: jevvy
description: Jevvy is a local Next.js playground for exercising TypeSafe AI decisions—compose a shared state with Choice, Score, and Noul questions, run them live with your own API key, and inspect typed answers—plus an arcade where Jev pilots a space shooter from text radar.

name: jev-ncr-demo

name: JevScout

name: pi-jev

name: intelliprompter

description: A local workspace for coordinating multiple Codex projects from one interface, recording recommended model and reasoning level per task, running separate sessions, tracking progress, verification, token usage, session costs, and AGENTS.md context.

name: typesafe-computer-use
description: A macOS computer-use tool that automates GUI interactions for roughly $0.0002 per step by OCR-ing the screen, classifying the next action with TypeSafe, and clicking.

name: jev-semgrep
description: jev-semgrep is a cross-language semantic grep that scores every line against a meaning you specify, letting you search English text in Japanese or vice versa and combine meanings with AND/OR/NOT logic for precise concept-based search.

name: experiments
description: Reproducible LLM experiment receipts: exact scripts, unedited logs, and method/caveat READMEs backing Product Compass claims, covering model benchmarks, cost and latency comparisons, benchmarks like a 105-bug coding rig and blind AI-slop judging.

name: jev-skill-gate
description: jev-skill-gate is a Node 18+ CLI that installs a SessionStart hook for Claude Code which scores installed skills against project signals using TypeSafe's Jev decision model (or a free local TF-IDF scorer), then writes skillOverrides to demote irrelevant skills to name-only or hidden states—cutting skill manifest tokens by ~75% for roughly $0.0005 per session while never writing `off`.

name: hermes-plugins
description: A monorepo of three independently installable PyPI plugins for the Hermes Agent CLI—hermes-ssh for registry-based multi-host SSH operations, hermes-sfw for routing npm/Python/Rust dependency installs through Socket Firewall Free, and hermes-jev-compact for Jev-scored context compression—with install, enable, and troubleshooting instructions.

name: jev-pruner
description: A Claude Code plugin that runs TypeSafe's Jev on Bash stdout exceeding ~10,000 estimated tokens, scoring line-chunks against session history to omit noise as `[N lines omitted]` markers while preserving diagnostics, whole documents, and a full-output archive—reducing context carried into later turns without summarizing.

name: Jev-cu
description: Jev-cu is an installable Codex skill plus scripts that delegate Computer Use's next-step choice to Jev, which selects element, action, completion, and risk from text-only UI candidates while Codex executes, behind a dry-run-first local policy gate requiring human confirmation for sensitive operations.

name: jev-rules
description: A Claude Code plugin that asks the Jev decision model, per prompt and per edited file, which of a project's Markdown rules and codebase-map documents apply, injecting only the matches in under a second and failing open to all rules on any error.

name: jev_local
description: A local API server that returns choice/score/noul probabilities for questions over text, JSON, and images in TypeSafe's `/v1/systemone` format, using either zero-shot LFM2.5 logprobs via llama.cpp or a fine-tuned ModernBERT-Ja cross-encoder backend.

name: jev-mermaid
description: A local Node.js demo that executes a Mermaid flowchart subset as ticket-routing logic, requesting typed Choice and Score judgments from Jev via `@typesafe-ai/sdk` and highlighting the computed route in the browser, with a fixture-backed Preview mode that works without an API key.

name: system-one-adapter-python
description: Drop-in replacement for typesafe_sdk's `system_one` evaluation API backed by OpenAI/Anthropic LLMs instead of TypeSafe, enabling cost/speed/intelligence comparisons with sync/async clients, structured outputs, probability normalization, retries, and usage/debug telemetry.

name: dify-plugin-typesafe-ai
description: A Dify Tool plugin for TypeSafe AI that provides Yes/No binary judgments with a tunable threshold and an Evaluate action batching typed noul/choice/score questions, exposing decisions, probabilities, and token usage as workflow variables over HTTPS to api.typesafe.ai.

name: localjev
description: LocalJev is a Bun/TypeScript server exposing a Jev-compatible `POST /v1/systemone` decision API that runs typed questions on DiffusionGemma through any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g. oMLX), prompting for JSON probabilities with validation, retries, normalization, and entropy-based confidence.

name: jev-drone
description: jev-drone provides a MuJoCo simulation of a camera-only autonomous drone with a small TypeSafe Jev judgment model in the loop at 2.5 Hz, useful for experimenting with vision-based autonomous flight and robotics control.

name: jot
description: Jot is a Node.js/TypeScript agent that runs the tool-calling loop for the Jev model — Jev picks tools and arguments while Jot executes calls, feeds results back into context, and iterates until a reply — shipping a chat UI with visible tool-call traces, a provider-independent core, and a loopback server that keeps credentials server-side and chats in the browser.

name: openclaw-smart-router
description: OpenClaw Smart Router is an OpenAI-compatible Fastify/TypeScript proxy that selects eligible Surplus Intelligence chat models using capability, cost, latency, history, preference, and jev classification signals while exposing metrics, feedback, routing history, dashboards, and hot-reloadable registries.

name: jev2048
description: jev2048 is a Playwright-powered CLI agent that shows low-latency constrained decision-making on real DOM-based 2048 sites: it reads the board, asks TypeSafe’s Jev model for one of four moves in one API call, presses the key, and reports calibrated probabilities.

name: pi-heed
description: pi-heed is a runtime guardrail for the pi coding agent that checks each side-effecting tool call against the user's conversational permissions and prohibitions, keeping structured policy state—including exceptions, lifts, and temporary grants—that survives context compaction.

name: jev-recall
description: jev-recall is a retrieval tool that filters an AI assistant's memories by semantic relevance rather than surface resemblance, using TypeSafe's Jev with embeddings and RAG techniques to surface pertinent context for LLM-powered agents, with a Next.js implementation.

name: jev-review
description: Jev Review is a local MCP server (stdio, Node.js 20+) that gives AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode a `jev_review` tool that submits a task, focused diff, and optional file context to the Jev API and returns per-dimension 1–10 quality scores with confidence levels, rubric hints, and deltas versus a previous evaluation, enabling a repeated score-driven improvement loop

name: pi-jev-compact
description: A Pi extension whose `/jev-compact` commands use TypeSafe's Jev model to selectively keep, truncate, or drop tool calls—and optionally assistant prose—then write a pruned new session plus an auditable HTML report, reclaiming context without lossy summaries.

name: is-jeven
description: is-jeven is a joke TypeScript/JavaScript package exposing an async `isEven(num, options?)` function that calls TypeSafe AI's Jev model to determine whether an integer is even, supporting API-key override and AbortSignal cancellation.

name: seems-lang
description: Seems is a Python superset language where `if` conditions can be plain-English judgments answered by the TypeSafe Jev API, with three-valued yes/no/unsure logic, lazy batched requests, caching, and line-preserving translation to ordinary Python.

name: jev-spring-boot-starter
description: A Spring Boot 4 starter that auto-configures TypeSafe Jev inside Spring MVC applications, wiring it together with RestClient so Jev can be used without manual setup.

name: s1decide
description: s1decide is a pre-alpha Apache-2.0 engine that answers typed questions (choice, score, true/false) about a state in one non-autoregressive forward pass over a shared prefilled cache, with masked logits forcing on-schema answers and published calibration.

name: TYPESAFE_JEV
description: Python demo tooling for TypeSafe AI's Jev "System One" endpoint, which returns typed decisions (choice, score, or yes/no probability) with calibrated confidence, including a user-upgrade triage script that repeats calls to measure stability and gates on confidence, plus seven example scenarios for routing uncertain cases to human review.

name: jev-chatbot
description: An experimental chatbot harness that turns TypeSafe’s non-generative Jev choice model into a next-word or reply selector over 30k words, with browser and Node CLI interfaces, seven comparison modes, cached embedding-built trees, and measured speed, cost, and quality tradeoffs.

name: jev-compare
description: jev-compare is a comparison utility that lets users evaluate differences between inputs, useful for quickly spotting discrepancies during development or review workflows.

name: typesafe-router-pipeline
description: An Open WebUI Pipelines function that classifies each chat message by cost tier and code-vs-text kind, then routes it through ordered OpenRouter/OrcaRouter model lists with failover—so simple prompts hit cheap models while complex ones reach stronger backends.

name: tax-doc-classifier
description: An open-source TypeScript library that classifies each PDF page of a tax document into 261 IRS form IDs and 7 page kinds with calibrated confidence scores—via one call to TypeSafe's Jev decision model against a generated JSON form registry—at $0.001/page, 34× cheaper and 6× faster than an LLM pipeline.

name: dag-jev
description: A Rust tool (`cargo run`) that reads test input from `input.txt`, renders dependency graphs via `render.sh` into `core/out`, and lets you verify its Jev output against control dependencies generated by `generate_control.py` using a `dep_{}_{}: 0/1` format.

name: jevgate
description: JevGate is a CLI that reviews selected source files with TypeSafe Jev for organization, simplification, and shared-logic concerns, offering reports, JSON output, context controls, role assessment, caching, and upload limits for iterative or CI checks.

name: jev-studio
description: Jev Studio is a Python kit for TypeSafe's Jev that provides a `jev` CLI for typed judgments (verify, screen, classify, extract, match, route, ask, find, rerank, compact, batch) plus a `jev-studio` MCP server exposing the Jev ruleset and instructions to MCP hosts over stdio.

name: triage-bot
description: A Node.js demo tool that triages support tickets in real time by using Jev's typed questions (choice/score/noul) to route each ticket to a specialist agent, score urgency, and decide on human escalation, then has Cerebras draft the reply with per-call latency timing.

name: jev-shogi
description: jev-shogi makes TypeSafe's judgment-only Jev model play shogi by passing all legal moves as probability-scored choices in one inference (no search engine), and ships v2/v3 lookahead variants, Fairy-Stockfish match results, KIF/mp4 game records, and calibration and replay-rendering scripts.

name: jev-gmail-ai-spam-filter-and-labeling
description: jevMail is a self-hosted Google Apps Script tool that uses the Jev AI model to label Gmail messages by meaning against custom natural-language criteria, with confidence-based second-pass review, optional auto-archiving, spend limits, and preview mode—no external backend required.

name: jev-commit
description: A commit-msg hook that sends the staged diff and message to TypeSafe's Jev decision model, which scores five checks—filler message, diff contradiction, debug leftovers, unmentioned work, secrets—and blocks only credentials (or findings under --strict), failing open on errors.

name: jev-audit
description: jev-audit is a zero-dependency, fully local CLI that scans a codebase for LLM call sites, flags those that are really decisions (classify, route, score, verify), and—via an installable agent skill—produces a JEV_AUDIT.md report tiering each call as Replace, Hybrid, Keep LLM, or Pure code with savings math, draft Jev question JSON, and a migration plan to TypeSafe AI's System One model.

name: jev-sandbox
description: A repo of six experiments testing when TypeSafe's Jev decision model can replace an LLM—covering email triage and gluten-label detection—with shared tooling for agreement, confidence-threshold, latency, and cost scoring plus reproducible run scripts and datasets.

name: jev-file-search
description: jev-file-search is a Python CLI that finds local files by content: a model triages filenames, types, and short text previews, then reads deeper only into uncertain files, keeping natural-language searches like "find subscription receipts, not credit top-ups" fast and cheap.

name: jevis
description: Jevis is a Dart package for Flutter's integration_test framework that uses TypeSafe's Jev model to drive UI tests: you register available actions, state a goal and action budget, and the model observes the current screen, picks the next action, and evaluates whether the goal is reached.

name: typesafe-ai-ruby
description: A dependency-free Ruby client for the TypeSafe System One API that sends state plus typed questions (yes/no Nouls, multi-option Choices, ordinal Scores) to the Jev model and returns structured answers with probabilities and confidence scores, plus retries, instrumentation, and per-call configuration.

name: codex-context-diet
description: A Codex plugin whose PostToolUse hook sends bulky tool results to TypeSafe's Jev for keep-or-drop verdicts, replacing stale output with a truncated head plus a one-line note so long sessions stop re-sending dead weight on every request.

name: gavel
description: An OpenClaw plugin exposing a `jev_decide` tool that lets agents make structured decisions — probabilities, option picks, and rubric scores with calibrated confidence — via TypeSafe's Jev model on OpenRouter in ~200ms for ~$0.00002, replacing slower, costlier LLM calls.

name: jev-reflex-autonomy-lab
description: An interactive multi-drone autonomy simulation where 1–15 drones steer via TypeSafe Jev System 1 reflexes that can asynchronously consult an optional OpenRouter System 2 planner when confidence drops, with seeded scenarios, per-drone telemetry, latency/confidence charts, and JSON export for comparing solo reflexes against guided flight.

name: ask-jev
description: Ask Jev provides an AskJev CLI, Dockerized stdio MCP server, and Astra skills that submit typed Noul, Choice, and Score checks to TypeSafe, letting agents validate interpretations, plans, edits, analyses, tool results, and completion claims against evidence during ongoing work.

name: pi-jev-wiki
description: pi-jev-wiki is an agent-managed wiki that maintains a project's conceptual space, using Jev to keep its accumulated knowledge legitimate, relevant, and robust as it scales.

name: pi-jev-guard
description: Pi extension that pre-reviews proposed code edits against Markdown-defined rules via the TypeSafe Jev API, reporting each violation's exact rule text and source line range, with an enforcement mode that blocks noncompliant writes within the configured repository scope.

name: typesafe4s
description: A Scala 3 SDK for TypeSafe's System One API that sends state and typed questions and returns typed answers with calibrated probabilities, exposing one shared runtime natively to ZIO, Cats Effect, Ox, Kyo, and Pekko with optional per-library JSON adapters.

name: jev_speedway
description: A dependency-free Node 20+ top-down racing game where a 60 fps physics simulation drives the cars while TypeSafe Jev judges each driver's worded situation every ~0.8 s, answering four questions (line, pace, overtake, boost) to demonstrate LLM-in-the-loop decision-making.

name: jev-robotics-demo
description: A MuJoCo simulation demo where a Franka arm with an Allegro hand stacks cubes, comparing an LLM agent that reasons step-by-step via low-level tools against Jev, a fast typed-probability model that picks pre-simulated moves — achieving the same result ~8x faster at ~1/1000th the cost.

name: jev-playground
description: MoonBit playground for TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model, bundling a typed API client with CLIs and experiments—single questions, Jev-vs-Jev Gomoku with real-time GIF replay, shell-risk gating, a 3v3 MOBA, an ESLint plugin, Claude Code permission hook, jevdsl/jevlang DSLs, and measured pattern reports.

name: hermes-jev-plugin
description: A Hermes Agent plugin exposing TypeSafe Jev’s calibrated Noul/Choice/Score judgments as four tools—jev_evaluate, jev_check, jev_route, jev_score—for batched atomic decisions, failure triage, review gates, task routing, and severity scoring in coding-agent workflows, plus a bundled question-design skill.

name: jev-one
description: Jev One is a TypeScript/ESM library for building stateful applications where TypeSafe AI's Jev model answers by pointing to developer-supplied choices—vocabularies, numbered items, capabilities, controls—whose effects a runtime applies and observes until a goal is verified.

name: invalidate
description: invalidate is a Python library that continuously checks every stored agent memory against each new event—using the ~150 ms, $0.00006-per-check Jev yes/no model plus fixed rules—to mark stale facts superseded or contradicted without editing them, route uncertain cases to human review, and layer onto existing stores like Mem0, Chroma, or pgvector so agents stop answering from outdated memories.

name: jev-java
description: jev-java is an idiomatic Java SDK for integrating the TypeSafe AI Jev System One decision engine, letting Java applications invoke and manage AI-powered decisions through a natural, Java-native API.

name: reaper
description: Reaper is a CLI semantic linter for coding agents that checks Git diffs or codebases and emits deterministic text/JSON diagnostics for semantic problems ordinary linters miss, like narrating comments, shallow abstractions, silent fallbacks, weakened assertions, and scope creep.
